target_customer: Clinicians, patients and drug developers in autoimmune disease
problem: Doctors cannot predict which treatment will work for a patient with an autoimmune disease such as IBD or rheumatoid arthritis.
business_model: Clinical lab tests and data partnerships with pharma

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining molecular, functional and clinical data into predictive tests needs genomics research and clinical validation.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary patient data could compound, but no evidence of validated product or exclusive data was found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Prometheus sold IBD response tests; no source shows what it did about Coral. Coral was later marked acquired or acquihired by an unnamed party.

market_need_then: Autoimmune patients often cycle through ineffective biologics; the need was real but no dated demand evidence was opened.

branding.domain_note: coralgenomics.com now redirects to an unrelated site.
branding.community_and_virality: Press from GenomeWeb and partnerships with Crohn's and Colitis Foundation (PRWeb 2022).

brand_strength.rationale: Short evocative name with trade press, but little evidence of brand impact.

outcome_analysis: Coral Genomics pursued predictive lab tests for autoimmune disease and partnered with patient groups, but funding was small and the acquirer, date and terms of its acquisition are not public. It may have been an acquihire, so the cause of the outcome cannot be determined from available sources.
notes: Website redirects to an unrelated domain, treated as dead. Aggregators report about 2M seed from Soma Capital, 8VC and YC, NIH SBIR grants, and totals from 2M to 5.7M; none verified by a primary source, so no rounds recorded. One directory says acquihired; unverified. Competitor evidence dated 2018 not found. Completeness pass: the seed of about 2M after demo day is reported by 360Dx/GenomeWeb (seen in a search snippet, page returned 403; date not given there, Seedtable dates a seed to 2019). Investors come from earlier notes and are not confirmed by that article. The NIH R44 grant of 1,205,206 for fiscal 2021 is from an NIH grant record naming Dixit as principal investigator. Other totals (CB Insights about 2M, Employbl and Seedtable 5.7M) conflict and were not summed; the history is likely incomplete.
